text: This summary does not contain all of the information you should consider before investing in our ordinary shares. You should read the entire prospectus carefully, including “Risk Factors,” “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations,” “Business” and our consolidated financial statements and the related notes included at the end of this prospectus, before making an investment in our ordinary shares.

We are a known one-stop workforce and human resources management solution provider focused on the sourcing, recruitment, deployment and ongoing management of legally employed workforce for corporate customers mainly serving manufacturing, construction, and service-based industries across Malaysia. We support employers that require scalable workforce in project-based and labor-intensive environments and that must comply with applicable workforce and employment-related requirements. Our services are designed to reduce administrative burden for customers and to improve workforce continuity through structured onboarding, worker management processes and compliance support.

With more than 15 years of proven industry experience, we specialize in delivering reliable, skilled, and committed teams that support every stage of our clients’ workforce needs. Our integrated approach is designed to ensure that our clients benefit from consistent quality, operational efficiency, and workforce solutions that align with their business goals.

We generate revenue principally by entering into service contracts with corporate customers under which we source casual workers and skilled temporary workers from our recruitment network and deploy them to perform specified tasks at the customer’s worksite or under the customer’s direction. …

sections.title: Use of Proceeds
text: Assuming a public offering price of $5.00 per share (the midpoint of the price range on the cover page of this prospectus), we estimate that the net proceeds to us from the sale of our ordinary shares in this offering will be approximately $16,585,000 (assuming no exercise of the over-allotment option) after deducting estimated underwriting discounts, the non-accountable expense allowance and estimated offering expenses payable by us. Each $1.00 increase (decrease) in the assumed public offering price will increase (decrease) the net proceeds to us from this offering by approximately $3,660,000 assuming the maximum number of ordinary shares offered by us, as set forth on the cover page of this prospectus, remains the same and after deducting estimated underwriting discounts, non-accountable expense allowance and estimated offering expenses payable by us. The as adjusted information discussed above is illustrative only and will be adjusted based on the actual public offering price and other terms of this offering determined at pricing.
We plan to use the net proceeds from this offering as follows:

• Business expansion through workforce expansion and strategic growth – We intend to use 40% of the proceeds from this offering to scale up existing core workforce management operations tapping into new geographical, emerging markets where there are rising demand for legal workforce supply while maintaining key management and operations base in Malaysia. We may use also use these proceeds to explore potential opportunities to strategically diversify our business by way of the acquisition of businesses with synergies in human resources (HR) technology, manpower outsourcing, or workforce-related logistics and investments in early-stage ventures which complement Kainan’s ecosystem (e.g., worker housing, training centers, digital HR platforms). We have not identified any targets for acquisition as of the date of this prospectus.

• Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Systems Upgrade – We intend to use 40% of the proceeds from this offering towards the acceleration of our digital transformation. Core components of same include: 1) upgrading our Workforce Management System to improve automation, compliance tracking, and reporting accuracy; 2) implementing integrated ERP/SAP modules for finance, HR, procurement, and operations; 3) enhancing our cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, and data governance; 4) improving our system scalability to handle larger worker volumes and expansion into new jurisdictions.
• Working Capital & Operational Reserves – We intend to use the remaining proceeds, if any, for general working capital and corporate purposes.

The foregoing represents our current intentions based upon our present plans and business conditions to use and allocate the net proceeds of this offering. Our management, however, will have significant flexibility and discretion to apply the net proceeds of this offering. If an unforeseen event occurs or business conditions change, we may use the proceeds of this offering differently than as described in this prospectus. See “Risk Factors.”

sections.title: Business
text: Our mission is to provide innovative, technology-driven workforce management solutions that enhance productivity, optimize labor supply, and drive sustainable growth for businesses in the construction, manufacturing, and cleaning industries. We are an integrated workforce and engineering solutions provider, recognized for our ability to build strong teams, deliver sustainable industrial water infrastructure, and support our clients with end-to-end solutions designed to drive long-term growth and operational excellence.

We are a one-stop workforce and human resources management solution provider, serving manufacturing, construction, and service-based industries across Malaysia. With more than 15 years of proven industry experience, we specialize in delivering reliable, skilled, and committed teams that support every stage of our clients’ workforce needs. Our integrated approach ensures that our clients benefit from consistent quality, operational efficiency, and workforce solutions that align with their business goals.

We generate revenue principally by entering into service contracts with corporate customers under which we source casual workers and skilled temporary workers from our recruitment network and deploy them to perform specified tasks at the customer’s worksite or under the customer’s direction. Revenue is recognized over time as the services are rendered and is determined by multiplying the number of attendance-confirmed work days (or hours, where applicable) for each deployed worker by the agreed workday pay rate set out in each customer contract. We invoice customers on a monthly basis following reconciliation of attendance and hours worked.

Since our inception, our business has generated significant growth in revenue. Our revenue increased from RM 81,268,230 for the year ended June 30, 2025, to RM108,991,616 equivalent to approximately USD26,700,543 for the year ended June 30, 2026, representing an increase of RM27,723,386 or approximately 34.1%. …

sections.title: Management
text: The following are our executive officers and directors and their respective ages and positions
*The individual consents to be in such position upon the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part.

Whitney Tan Ann Nee. Since June 2025, Ms. Whitney Tan has served as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Kainan Holding Group Ltd, where she leads the Company’s strategy and operations with a strong focus on sustainable growth, governance, and a people-first culture. During the initial stage of the Company’s operating subsidiary, Ms. Whitney Tan served as Managing Director, where she was responsible for the overall management of the business, including operations, branding and marketing, as well as business expansion and development. Currently, Ms. Whitney Tan is primarily responsible for the formulation of business strategies, including corporate plans, branding and marketing strategies, and contributing to the growth of the Company. Since founding Kainan Sdn. Bhd. in August 2009, Ms. Whitney Tan has accumulated more than 15 years of experience in the human resources and contractor industries. Ms. Whitney Tan has successfully expanded the business from a foreign workforce solutions provider into an integrated EPCC contractor offering technical, procurement, management, and HR capabilities, while establishing strategic partnerships with industry partners and stakeholders. Ms. Whitney Tan also plays a vital role and actively champions corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives that support underprivileged communities. She completed an Executive Master in Industrial Human Resources Management in 2025. She was awarded the Outstanding Female Elite Award and Outstanding Growth Award by China Press Malaysia and is accredited by the Malaysia Ministry of Human Resources. Based upon her extensive experience in the industry, the Company believes that Ms. Whitney Tan is well qualified to serve as the Chief Executive Officer.

sections.title: Enforcement of Civil Liabilities
text: We are incorporated under the laws of the British Virgin Islands, and our officers and directors are residents outside the United States. Moreover, a majority of our consolidated assets are located outside the United States. Although we are incorporated outside the United States, we have agreed to accept service of process in the United States through our agent designated for that purpose. Nevertheless, substantially all of the consolidated assets owned by us are located outside the United States and any judgment obtained in the United States against us may not be enforceable outside the United States. There is no treaty between the United States and the British Virgin Islands providing for the reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters and a final judgment for the payment of money rendered by any federal or state court in the United States based on civil liability, whether or not predicated solely upon the federal securities laws, would, therefore, not be automatically enforceable in the British Virgin Islands. There is uncertainty as to whether judgments of courts in the United States based upon the civil liability provisions of the federal securities laws of the United States would be recognized or enforceable in the British Virgin Islands. In making a determination as to enforceability of a judgment of the courts of the United States, the BVI courts would have regard to whether the judgment was final and conclusive and on the merits of the case, given by a court of law of competent jurisdiction, and was expressed to be for a fixed sum of money. …

These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company’s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company’s financial statements based on our audits. We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. summary: Our holding company structure makes us dependent on the operations of our subsidiaries.

Our key customers for our manpower outsourcing business contribute to a significant portion of our revenues in each of these business segments. A non-renewal of these contracts could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We depend on a small number of individuals who constitute our current management.
Our industry is subject to extensive government regulation and the imposition of additional regulations could materially harm our future earnings.
We may not be able to maintain and/or obtain approvals, licenses and registrations necessary to carry on or expand our business.
Changes in foreign worker regulations and licensing requirements could materially and adversely affect our ability to fulfill customer requisitions, cost structure and results of operations.
We may from time to time be subject to legal and regulatory proceedings and administrative investigations.
Misconduct and errors by our employees could harm our business and reputation.
We may not be able to pay any dividends on our ordinary shares in the future due to BVI law.
As the rights of shareholders under British Virgin Islands law differ from those under U.S. law, you may have fewer protections as a shareholder.
British Virgin Islands companies may not be able to initiate shareholder derivative actions, thereby depriving shareholders of the ability to protect their interests.

The laws of the British Virgin Islands may provide less protection for minority shareholders than those under U.S. law, so minority shareholders may have less recourse than they would under U.S. law if the shareholders are dissatisfied with the conduct of our affairs.

We will be a foreign private issuer and, as a result, we will not be subject to U.S. proxy rules and will be subject to Exchange Act reporting obligations that, to some extent, are more lenient and less detailed than those of a U.S. issuer.

As a foreign private issuer and as permitted by the listing requirements of Nasdaq, we may follow certain BVI corporate governance rules instead of certain corporate governance requirements of Nasdaq.

We may lose our foreign private issuer status, which would then require us to comply with the Exchange Act’s domestic reporting regime and cause us to incur additional legal, accounting and other expenses.

We are a BVI-incorporated company with substantially all of our assets located in Malaysia, and it may be difficult to enforce a judgment of U.S. courts for civil liabilities under U.S. federal securities laws against us, our directors or officers.

Subject to the general authority to allot and issue new ordinary shares provided by our shareholders, under British Virgin Island law our directors may allot and issue new ordinary shares on terms and conditions and for such purposes as may be determined by our Board in its sole discretion.
We will likely not pay dividends in the foreseeable future.

There has been no existing market for our ordinary shares, and we do not know whether one will develop to provide you with adequate liquidity. If the trading price of our ordinary shares fluctuates after this offering, you could lose a significant part of your investment.
The price of our ordinary shares may rapidly fluctuate or may decline regardless of our operating performance, resulting in substantial losses for investors.

Certain recent initial public offerings of companies with relatively small public floats have experienced extreme volatility that was seemingly unrelated to the underlying performance of the respective company. Our ordinary shares may potentially experience rapid and substantial price volatility, which may make it difficult for prospective investors to assess the value of our ordinary shares.

As a company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands, we are permitted to adopt certain home country practices in relation to corporate governance matters that differ significantly from Nasdaq corporate governance listing standards. These practices may afford less protection to shareholders than they would enjoy if we complied fully with Nasdaq corporate governance listing standards.

If we were deemed to be an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, applicable restrictions could make it impractical for us to continue our business as contemplated and could have a material adverse effect on our business and the price of our ordinary shares.

Our Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Whitney Tan Ann Nee will beneficially own more than 50.00% of our outstanding ordinary shares after this offering, and this concentration of ownership and voting power will limit your ability to influence corporate matters.
As a “controlled company” under the rules of Nasdaq, we may choose to exempt our company from certain corporate governance requirements that could have an adverse effect on our public shareholders.
If securities or industry analysts do not publish research, or publish inaccurate or unfavorable research, about our business, the price of our ordinary shares and our trading volume could decline.
Future sales of ordinary shares, or the perception of such future sales, by some of our existing shareholders could cause our share price to decline.
New investors in our ordinary shares will experience immediate and substantial dilution after this offering.

In the future, our ability to raise additional capital to expand our operations and invest in our business may be limited, and our failure to raise additional capital, if required, could impair our business.

ocf.heading: Operating activities
ocf.text:
Net cash generated from operating activities in 2025 was RM8,014,893, which consists of our profit before tax of RM5,762,113 as adjusted for non-cash items and non-operating items, changes in operating activities and cash used in operations. Adjustments for non-cash items consisted of depreciation of property and equipment of RM720,504, investment property of RM22,000, fair value changes on financial assets through profit of RM13,331, gain on derecognition of lease liabilities of RM 388. Adjustments for non-operating items consisted of finance cost of RM1,403,240, provision of ECL on trade receivables of RM219,437 and interest income of RM9,057. Changes in operating assets and liabilities mainly included: (i) a decrease in trade and other receivables of RM3,687,303; (ii) an decrease in other payables and accruals of RM2,908,338; and (iii) a decrease in amount due to directors of RM73,442. Cash used in operations included income tax payment of RM795,148.

Net cash used in operating activities in 2026 was RM2,998,571 (approximately USD734,584), which consisted of our profit before tax of RM6,318,779 (approximately USD1,547,963), as adjusted for non-cash items and non-operating items, changes in operating activities and cash used in operations.

sm.heading: Selling and marketing expenses
sm.text: Selling and marketing expenses primarily comprise costs related to advertising, marketing and branding activities. For the year ended June 30, 2026, selling and marketing expenses increased by RM390,936, or approximately 51.4%, from RM759,865 for the year ended June 30, 2025 to RM1,150,801 (approximately USD281,921) for the year ended June 30, 2026. The increase was mainly attributable to increased marketing and branding efforts to promote our services and enhance brand visibility. We expect marketing and branding activities to continue to increase as part of our strategic growth initiatives.

ga.heading: General and administrative expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses primarily consist of employee benefit expenses, rental expenses, depreciation, professional service fees, office expenses, transportation, legal fees and expenses related to legal claims, and other administrative costs. For the year ended June 30, 2026, general and administrative expenses increased by RM3,243,015, or approximately 97.4%, from RM3,330,122 for the year ended June 30, 2025 to RM6,573,137 (approximately USD1,610,273) for the year ended June 30, 2026. The increase was mainly attributable to higher employee benefit expenses, professional service fees, legal fees and expenses incurred in connection with legal claims during the year, as well as increased administrative and operating costs to support the Company’s business expansion and growth in revenue. The Company also incurred higher costs associated with its ongoing business development and corporate activities during the year.

nonop.heading: Other income
nonop.text:
For the year ended June 30, 2026, other income increased by RM73,484, or approximately 12.9%, from RM570,370 for the year ended June 30, 2025 to RM643,854 (approximately USD157,730). The increase was primarily attributable to a gain on disposal of property, plant and equipment of RM100,150, compared to nil in 2025, and higher sundry income of RM79,916, which mainly comprised referral fees received from a developer and excess collections from customers relating to statutory contributions. This increase was partially offset by the compensation income of RM80,000 and income from the sale of wood products of RM34,682 recognized in 2025, which were non-recurring in nature and were not recognized in 2026. In addition, fixed deposit interest income increased from RM9,057 in 2025 to RM14,087 in 2026, while fair value gains on financial assets at fair value through profit or loss increased from RM13,331 to RM18,412. Rental income decreased slightly by RM6,950, from RM430,550 in 2025 to RM423,600 in 2026.

For the year ended June 30, 2026, other expenses decreased by RM264,193, or approximately 74.4%, from RM355,006 for the year ended June 30, 2025 to RM90,813 (approximately USD22,247).
